audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 1, 2 and 3 disagree with the packet and with their own prose. Rows 1 and 2 print Jax above whys that say "it stays skill-based" and "still a coin-flip"; row 3 prints Skill above whys[3] "your Q poke and short trades exploit Jax".
audit.why: Packet chart is Skill, Skill, Skill, Zaahen, Skill, Jax, Jax, with no defects flagged. The mirror audit records rows 1, 2 and 3 corrected in both layers as one atomic group, with phases[3] rewritten to state the level 4-5 advantage instead of generic lane-control filler.
audit.corrected: Rows 1 and 2 to Skill, row 3 to Zaahen, in both layers as matched pairs, with phases[3].rating raised to 6/10 (the inverse of the mirror's 4/10) and the three whys backed by real cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page names Counter Strike as the tracked cooldown in twelve fields and never states it. packet.sequencingCues is 8, so the prose gestures at timing constantly without a single number.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9 — seventeen seconds at rank 1, the longest lane cooldown in this matchup by a wide margin and the entire reason levels 4-5 belong to Zaahen. Empower is 7/6/5/4/3, Leap Strike 8/7.5/7/6.5/6, and Grandmaster-at-Arms is 110/100/90 — identical to Grim Deliverance at rank 1, so the level 6 fight is a straight cooldown race neither of you wins.
audit.corrected: The 17s, 7s and 110s written into phases[1], phases[2], phases[3], every spike, early, mid, late and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: (a) "Grandmaster's Might" is not the ability — it is Grandmaster-at-Arms. (b) "Golden Onslaught" (Aureate Rush) and "Final Retribution" (Grim Deliverance) again. (c) Counter Strike is described as blanket negation — "his E dodge blanks your Q", "negates your Q's poke value" — with no distinction between attacks and abilities. (d) Empower's auto-attack reset is absent.
audit.why: The kit says Counter Strike lets him "dodge all incoming attacks". Zaahen's Q empowers his next attack, so yes, it gets dodged — but Aureate Rush is a dash that slices around him, not an attack, so it still lands. Telling the player their whole kit is blanked leads them to disengage when they should be dashing in. missingInteractions flags Empower as the auto-reset that opens his combo, and at 7s at rank 1 that wind-up is the most repeated tell in the lane.
audit.corrected: Real names throughout, the attacks-not-abilities distinction stated, and the Empower wind-up named as the step-back cue.

edits.after: Level 2 stays even: neither of you forces a clean trade, and Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1 once he spends it.

edits.after: Level 3 is still a coin-flip — hold the wave near your side so Jax has to walk into your range to use it.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Counter Strike's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are yours: Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1, so poke The Darkin Glaive into that gap before his E-W all-in comes online.

edits.before: Your window: before Jax has both E (Counter Strike) and enough levels to trade, land Q (Darkin Glaive) at max range and back off, punishing any last-hit walk-up. Once he hits Lvl 4-5 with points in E and W (Empower), his all-in gets real, so don't linger in his stun range.
edits.after: Your window: Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1, so land The Darkin Glaive on his walk-up and back off inside that gap. Empower (W) is his auto-attack reset on 7s — the wind-up, not the cast, is your cue to step back, and by 4-5 the E into W all-in is real.

edits.before: Jax R (Grandmaster's Might) hands him a burst of resists and on-hit damage that flips even trades; when he ults into your E (Golden Onslaught) he can tank the strike and win the melee. Only commit R (Final Retribution) if his E is on cooldown.
edits.after: Grandmaster-at-Arms gives him resists and on-hit damage that flip even trades, and it is 110s — exactly your Grim Deliverance. Commit yours only while Counter Strike sits on its 17s, or Aureate Rush arrives into a stun instead.

edits.after: Jax pulls ahead here: Blade of the Ruined King or Trinity plus his passive attack speed outpaces your dueling, and Counter Strike dodges attacks — so The Darkin Glaive is blanked by it, but Aureate Rush is not.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are neutral farm; neither of you has the tools to commit, so trade autos only when his E is on cooldown and respect his level-2 W empower spike.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are neutral farm; neither of you can commit yet, so trade only inside Counter Strike's 17s and respect the level-2 Empower spike — a 7s auto reset.

edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a real window: Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1, so poke and short-trade inside it before his E-W all-in is online. At 6 Grandmaster-at-Arms flips the extended fight back.

edits.after: Poke with The Darkin Glaive (Q) while Counter Strike is down

edits.before: - Jax Counter Strike: matchup-defining — Dodges autos + stuns. Bait it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Counter Strike (E): 17s at rank 1 — it dodges attacks, not abilities, so Aureate Rush still lands. - Empower (W): 7s auto reset. - Grim Deliverance (R): 110s, the same as his Grandmaster-at-Arms.

edits.after: Dodges attacks and stuns, 17s at rank 1. Commit once it is spent.

edits.before: Your R is the kill window — build your teamfight around that. Jax carry threat: 10/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.

notes: Best single fact recovered here: Counter Strike is 17 seconds at rank 1. The page tracked it in twelve fields as the matchup-defining cooldown without ever saying how long it is, and it is long enough that the whole levels 4-5 window exists because of it. Second: the page said his E 'blanks your Q' and left it there — it dodges attacks, so The Darkin Glaive (an empowered attack) is dodged but Aureate Rush (a dash that slices) is not, which is the difference between disengaging and committing. Fabricated names fixed: 'Grandmaster's Might' for Grandmaster-at-Arms, plus the recurring 'Golden Onslaught' and 'Final Retribution' for Zaahen's E and R — now nine matchups in a row carrying at least one of those two.
